rejected.title: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy
card: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a disease of the brain. It is linked to repeated knocks to the head over many years.
Repeated head knocks happen in contact sports such as boxing, football and rugby. They can also happen in other settings, such as military service.
CTE can affect memory, mood and behaviour. Signs often appear years after the knocks, and they can be similar to those of other brain conditions.
A certain diagnosis needs the brain tissue itself to be examined, which can happen only after death. Current tests and scans in a living person cannot confirm it.
rejected.remember: Repeated head knocks are linked to CTE, but only an examination of the brain tissue after death can confirm it.

a.q: Why can doctors not give a living person a certain diagnosis of CTE?
opts: Proof needs the brain tissue itself to be examined
Its signs are always the same as those of a stroke
It shows signs only in people aged over 80
It is caused by a single blow that leaves no trace
a.why: A certain diagnosis of CTE needs the brain tissue to be examined, and that can happen only after death. The signs are not the same as a stroke's every time; they can be similar to other conditions, which is why signs alone are not enough.
a.clue: Think about what part of the brain must be looked at, and when.

b.q: Dan played rugby for 20 years. In his fifties he has memory problems and mood changes, and his doctor suspects CTE. Which statement is correct?
opts: CTE is possible, but it cannot be confirmed in life
CTE is possible, and a brain scan now can confirm it
CTE is unlikely, as he never had a single big injury
CTE is unlikely, as it affects movement, not mood
b.why: Years of repeated head knocks are linked to CTE, and memory and mood changes fit its signs, so CTE is possible. A brain scan seems a sensible way to check, but current tests in a living person cannot confirm CTE. Only an examination of the brain tissue after death can.
b.clue: Can any test on a living person confirm CTE?
